contributions.summary: Hierarchical clustering + PCA identifies six named cooperation structures from passing network.
900-second sliding window captures temporal dynamics of network performance indicators.
Creative taxonomy of six cooperation patterns with tactical interpretation.
Data-driven formation recommendation (4-4-2) with Absolute Suppress vulnerability warning.
Analogy-based extension of sports cooperation analysis to general teamwork.

assumptions.summary: All teams play at full strength regardless of weather/luck.
Athlete skill level remains constant throughout season.
Match results absolutely fair (no false balls/black whistles).
Players fully implement coach tactics and strategy.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: MCM-provided passing event data: passer, receiver, coordinates, timestamps for 38 matches.
1352 cooperation structures extracted (passes > 5); 7 abnormal removed; 1345 valid.
38 matches split: 19 for model setup, 19 for universality evaluation.

models.summary: Cooperation Structure Network: directed graph + hierarchical clustering + PCA -> six structure types.
Sliding Window Performance: 900s window, ANC and transitivity time series.
Strategic Recommendation: frequency comparison + PageRank -> formation advice.

verification.summary: Match 15 (2:0 win): Huskies ANC consistently above opponent; empirical support.
Match 23 (0:4 loss): opponent transitivity dominates; negative case confirmation.
19-match evaluation set: cooperation structure usage patterns hold across second half of season.
Absolute Suppress threat: 0W 1D 3L record when opponents use this structure.

results_trace.summary: model output: six cooperation structures -> interpretation: named taxonomy with tactical meaning.
model output: ANC time series -> visual: Huskies above opponent -> answer: better coordination.
model output: transitivity time series -> visual: opponent dominates -> answer: explains 0:4 defeat.
model output: frequency comparison -> interpretation: Huskies favor defensive counterattack (Long Ball).
model output: structure analysis -> answer: 4-4-2 formation, counter-attack strategy, sidewalk development.

weaknesses.summary: High time complexity O(m^2 log m) for hierarchical clustering.
Slight window size distortion from discrete event timestamps.
No statistical significance test for frequency differences.
Analogy-based generalization without any supporting data.
PageRank used for squad selection without specifying parameters.
K=6 cluster count chosen by dendrogram inspection; no sensitivity analysis.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Directed passing network confirms network-based team analysis pattern.
Hierarchical clustering produces network indicators for cooperation structure identification.
Sliding window temporal analysis captures dynamic network performance.
Four bullet assumptions with fairness and compliance.

independent_extensions.summary: Sliding window model reusable for any temporal network indicator analysis.
Cooperation structure taxonomy via clustering applicable to other team sports.
Creative naming convention for structure types aids interpretability.
Train-test split (19/19 matches) for model universality evaluation.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Six creatively named cooperation structures likely impressed judges with interpretability.
Sliding window model is original contribution with clear photograph metaphor.
Actionable coaching advice with specific formation recommendation demonstrates practical value.

source_quality.notes: Text extraction clean; some Unicode garbling in mathematical notation on pages 10-11.

task_reconstruction.problem_statement: Build a network-based model to identify cooperation patterns in soccer passing data, evaluate performance with temporal indicators, and provide coaching advice.
sub_tasks: Problem 1: Identify cooperation structures from passing network
Problem 2: Develop performance indicators using network metrics
task_reconstruction.data_provided: Passing event data (passer, receiver, coordinates, timestamps) for 38 Huskies matches.

unresolved_questions: Why K=6 chosen without sensitivity analysis on cluster count?
